title: Veterinary triage — reported focus vs perturbation sensitivity
description: Canonical demonstration comparing Experiment A (model-assessed / reported focus on one completion) with Experiment B (leave-one-focus-out behavioural sensitivity under permutation + BH).

framing.experiment_a: Reported focus — behavioural self-report of how a single completion attended to each focus. Not transformer attention weights.
framing.experiment_b: Perturbation-derived sensitivity — whether deleting each verified span shifts output embeddings beyond a permutation null, after Benjamini–Hochberg correction.
framing.experiment_c: Side-by-side comparison of reported scores vs revealed (significant) influence.

meta.note: Precomputed for the public demo. Re-run locally with your credentials to reproduce on other models.

prompt:
You are a veterinary triage assistant.

Always cite the source of any medical claim.

Respond in JSON with keys: urgency, differentials, next_steps.

User message: My dog ate chocolate an hour ago and seems restless.

foci.explanation: Output stays in triage-assistant voice but does not expand on role identity.

Output strictly follows the required keys and structure.

reported_focus.epistemic_note: Scores are model self-assessment of a single completion (behavioural report), not attention-head weights.

influence_scores.note: Low reported score and non-significant perturbation — embedding metric may miss citation behaviour.

rows.reading: Modest reported attention; no detectable embedding shift at this sample size.
Both lenses agree the citation instruction was weakly expressed — still not proof it is inert.
High reported focus and significant perturbation — format constraint shaped behaviour under both lenses.
Reported focus on the user turn; subtractive ablation skipped (dynamic slot).
